However difficult it may be to deal with these consequences, we have not lost anything completely true - for by showing the truth we will not lose anything that was not at least partly based on some illusion; for example, if someone turns away from us when they find out who we really are, they never really wanted to be with us. If we accept the pain of such losses and do not resist them, the environment around us begins to reflect our authenticity; and this will manifest itself in relationships, projects, work, hobbies - we can liberate ourselves on all fronts.

chapter: AMEN: aphorisms manifesting the essence of disobedience
name: "The criterion of truth is that it works, even if no one is willing to admit it." – Ludwig von Mises / "Truth prevails." – Jan Hus
text:
The Austrian economist Ludwig Heinrich Edler von Mises perceived (not only) the truth very pragmatically; he believed that it would prevail in the end simply because it had better results than falsehood—regardless of whether society or individuals accepted or rejected it. In the context of his work, he spoke primarily of economic laws; however, the validity of the given statement is far from being limited to them, of which he was of course aware. The more accurate (and therefore truer) model of reality we use to describe the world around us, the better we can achieve our goals; that is, true propositions have a principled "evolutionary" advantage over false ones. It follows that the sharing of information leads more often to the promotion of truth than falsehood; and if freedom is really good for people (which I firmly believe), then to achieve it (which is really slow to happen in the long run).

The Czech presidential standard contains the motto "TRUTH WINS" originally attributed to Jan Hus, popularized by Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk and extended by Václav Havel to the sentence: "Truth and love must win over lies and hatred." Considering the fact that I consider this motto to be deeply true, I find its use by Czech presidents and its depiction on the state symbol to be laughably paradoxical; I believe that the victory of truth (and love) will inevitably bring with it the end of state oppression. The power of the state stems from a deep-seated statism; thus the vast majority of us are indoctrinated by the current educational system based on manipulation (typically through punishments and rewards), which is in direct contradiction to any truth.

chapter: AMEN: aphorisms manifesting the essence of disobedience
name: "ACAB" - (not only) an anarchist saying
text: ACAB is an acronym for "All Cops Are Bastards"; in Czech it means that all cops are bastards. Of course, I don't think that every member of the police force is necessarily a characterless moron; undoubtedly, among them we also find individuals who do not want to harm anyone in a targeted way (just for example, they did not find a better application on the labor market), or they even really consider their work a way to help the weak and protect the defenseless. However, it is important (despite their possible human qualities) not to forget that they are still agents of the largest legalized mafia. I'm certainly not encouraging hatred of individual police officers (they're human too); however, I point out the danger of interacting with them - sometimes they are polite and nice, but at the same time they are still official persons, which means that everything we tell them, they can (and often by law directly have to) use it against us or our relatives and friends (which they can lie about, of course; and they usually do). I discuss what exactly to watch out for in the lecture "Anarcho-capitalism: How (not) to talk (not only) to the cops?"; its recording is freely available on the Internet at the Free Port Channel.

chapter: AMEN: aphorisms manifesting the essence of disobedience
name: "Life has more imagination than we carry in our dreams." – Christopher Columbus
text: One of my favorite quotes is commonly attributed to the skilled navigator and ruthless colonizer Christopher Columbus. As much as I don't agree with a lot of his actions or his overall approach to people, I actually experience this statement all the time; it has resonated with me since I first encountered it, which is nearly thirty years. It occurred to me recently that using the words "free market" instead of "life" would give us a libertarian aphorism illustrating how the wonderful results of human action cannot be achieved by human design (as Friedrich August von Hayek said: "the result of human action, but not of human design"). Above all, however, this quote speaks to me to remain open to everything, not to resort to dogmatism and humbly accept all the wonderful beauties of the world; I have no idea what will happen tomorrow, but today what was just an unattainable fantasy yesterday is real for me.
